question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: Minimizing the physical pain experienced by the patient
options.B: Ensuring procedures do no harm to recipients, providers, and communities
options.C: Accelerating the speed at which medications are absorbed
options.D: Reducing the overall cost of purchasing disposable syringes

explanation: Injection safety focuses holistically on protecting patients, health workers, and the public from preventable biological hazards. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is rigorous training in injection safety particularly critical for student nurses?

options.A: It is the only way to pass mandatory licensing board examinations without remediation
options.B: It establishes a lifelong standard of safe, accountable clinical habits early in their career
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never experience localized bruising or swelling
options.D: It eliminates the need to wear sterile gloves during subcutaneous drug delivery

explanation: Building proper muscle memory and adherence to safety protocols during training prevents dangerous shortcuts in later practice. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: The scope of injection safety concludes with which of the following actions?

options.A: Obtaining verbal consent before the procedure begins
options.B: Documenting the drug batch number in the patient chart
options.C: Applying a dry cotton swab over the puncture site
options.D: Immediate, secure containment of the used sharp device

explanation: The safety cycle finishes only when sharps are safely deposited into a puncture-resistant container to prevent secondary injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: What happens to an injection procedure if a single step in the safety chain fails?

options.A: It remains safe as long as the medication itself is sterile
options.B: The patient is protected provided they have received past vaccinations
options.C: Only the healthcare provider faces a risk of blood exposure
options.D: The entire procedure is classified as unsafe and hazardous

explanation: Injection safety relies on an unbroken chain of precautions; a failure anywhere compromises the integrity of the whole process. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what defines a safe injection?

options.A: A technique that utilizes glass ampoules rather than plastic multi-dose vials
options.B: An injection that harms no one, exposes providers to no avoidable risk, and creates safe waste
options.C: A subcutaneous procedure performed exclusively by registered nurses
options.D: An intervention costing less than standard oral medication therapies

explanation: The WHO definition emphasizes three pillars: protection of the patient, protection of the healthcare worker, and safe waste management. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why do regulatory health frameworks strictly discourage the manual recapping of used needles?

options.A: It alters the chemical composition of the remaining medication in the barrel
options.B: It prevents the proper sterilization of reusable stainless steel syringes
options.C: It is the leading mechanical cause of accidental occupational needle-stick injuries
options.D: It delays the administration time during emergency resuscitation scenarios

explanation: Attempting to guide a needle back into its cap frequently results in the hand slipping and puncturing the skin, transmitting pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following bloodborne viruses poses the highest risk of transmission through a single needle-stick injury?
explanation: Hepatitis B has a significantly higher concentration in blood and viral stability, making it the most easily transmitted pathogen via sharps injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient develops a warm, fluctuant, and extremely painful swelling at the site of a previous intramuscular injection given a week ago. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Accidental puncture of a deep subcutaneous nerve branch
options.B: Introduction of bacteria due to a breach in aseptic technique
options.C: Rapid absorption of the drug into the surrounding adipose tissue
options.D: A normal localized hypersensitivity reaction to the preservative

explanation: A localized collection of pus or abscess formation typically indicates bacterial contamination introduced during the injection process. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the correct method for applying an alcohol swab to skin prior to an injection?

options.A: From the outer perimeter directly toward the center of the site
options.B: In a circular motion starting from the center and moving outward
options.C: Vertically up and down along the expected path of the needle
options.D: In a rigorous back-and-forth scrubbing motion across the muscle fibers

explanation: Starting at the center and moving outward sweeps mechanical contaminants away from the clean puncture zone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is it unacceptable to use the same syringe for multiple patients if you change the needle between them?

options.A: Syringes lose their vacuum seal and cannot draw accurate medication dosages
options.B: The syringe barrel and plunger can become contaminated with blood or fluids during use
options.C: New needles are manufactured with different threading that does not fit old barrels
options.D: Regulatory laws permit multi-patient syringes only in surgical operating theatres

explanation: Backflow into the barrel during aspiration or injection contaminates the internal components, making the syringe unsafe for another person regardless of a needle change. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: At what capacity should a sharps disposal container be permanently sealed and replaced?

options.B: At the end of every individual nursing shift
options.C: Completely packed to the absolute brim
options.D: One-quarter full to ensure lightweight handling

explanation: Sealing containers at three-quarters capacity prevents protruding needles and accidental punctures from overfilled openings. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary operational hazard of placing a sharps container far away from where injections are administered?

options.A: It causes the sterile medication inside the syringe to degrade from light exposure
options.B: It violates international medication dosage calculation formulas
options.C: It prevents accurate documentation of the injection time in the patient record
options.D: It forces staff to walk with exposed needles, drastically increasing the risk of a needle-stick injury

explanation: Sharps containers must be kept immediately accessible to prevent hazardous transit of uncapped needles across clinical spaces. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)
